subsystems.name: Space observatory
subsystems.role: provides a stable platform above the atmosphere for continuous monitoring of a star's brightness.

subsystems.name: Photometric or spectroscopic instrument
subsystems.role: records the combined light of star and planet with low noise over time.

subsystems.name: Time-series data pipeline
subsystems.role: turns raw detector counts into a calibrated light curve.

subsystems.name: Orbital and phase model
subsystems.role: fits the periodic brightness variation to isolate the planet's signal.

subsystems.name: Atmospheric retrieval
subsystems.role: infers temperature distribution, albedo, clouds and winds from the phase curve.
parts: prior knowledge of planet and star

buildSteps.title: Select a target
buildSteps.detail: Choose a short-period, highly irradiated planet so the planet's own light is a measurable fraction of the total.

buildSteps.title: Plan the observation
buildSteps.detail: Schedule the telescope to stare at the star continuously for one or more full orbits, avoiding gaps that would blur the phase curve.

buildSteps.title: Acquire the light curve
buildSteps.detail: Record total flux over time with a photometer or spectrograph, often across several wavelengths.

buildSteps.title: Remove systematics
buildSteps.detail: Correct for detector drifts, pointing jitter and stellar variability such as starspots or faculae.

buildSteps.title: Fold and combine
buildSteps.detail: Phase-fold the data on the known orbital period and merge multiple orbits into a single average curve.

buildSteps.title: Measure the shape
buildSteps.detail: Extract the amplitude (day–night contrast), the phase offset (hot-spot shift from winds) and any asymmetries caused by clouds.

buildSteps.title: Interpret with models
buildSteps.detail: Fit atmospheric models to infer heat redistribution efficiency, Bond albedo and wind-driven energy transport.

prerequisites.tech: Space telescopes with stable, long-duration pointing
prerequisites.why: the signal is a tiny periodic variation that requires uninterrupted, precise photometry.
the planet's thermal emission peaks in the infrared for hot planets.
the phase must be referenced to a known orbital period to combine data correctly.
they translate a phase curve into physical quantities like temperature contrast and winds.

pathway.milestone: phase curves of hot Jupiters and warm Neptunes measured by space telescopes such as Hubble, Spitzer, JWST and CHEOPS
pathway.unlocks: a working picture of day–night heat transport and cloud behaviour in highly irradiated atmospheres.

pathway.milestone: multi-wavelength phase curves of smaller planets with JWST and future dedicated missions
pathway.unlocks: separation of cloud, haze and gas contributions, and comparison across planet types.

pathway.milestone: three-dimensional mapping of clouds and winds from phase-curve and eclipse data combined
pathway.unlocks: direct constraints on atmospheric circulation and weather patterns.

pathway.milestone: phase curves of temperate rocky planets from next-generation space telescopes
pathway.unlocks: assessment of habitability through global energy balance and surface conditions.
